capture.final_message:
Use the realization of the compact-convergence uniformity as uniform convergence on compact subsets.

For the first conjunct, compactness of `α` makes the single compact set `univ` cofinal among all compact subsets. Thus a basis `V i` for the uniformity of `β` lifts directly to the entourages
\[
\{(f,g)\mid \forall x,\ (f(x),g(x))\in V_i\}
\]
of `C(α,β)`.

For the second conjunct, the equality on the left is the definitional coercion property of `ContinuousMap.toUniformOnFunIsCompact`, so it is immediate. The substantive right side follows by combining the compact exhaustion with the antitone basis of `β`. First obtain a two-parameter basis: uniform control by `V_n` on a compact set `K_m`. Every compact subset is contained in some stage of the exhaustion. Then diagonalize the indices: replacing `(m,n)` by `r = max m n` strengthens both requirements, since `K_m ⊆ K_r` and antitonicity gives `V_r ⊆ V_n`. Consequently the diagonal entourages
\[
W_r=\{(f,g)\mid \forall x\in K_r,\ (f(x),g(x))\in V_r\}
\]
are cofinal in the compact-convergence uniformity. They are themselves antitone because the exhaustion grows while the target entourages shrink. This proves the right side and hence the stated equivalence.
